_comment: This roster is empty on purpose, and an entry added here would not run.
The cron ticker lives in the gateway, and only the `default` (Chat Agent)
profile has one. This profile is reached through the kanban dispatcher,
which spawns a worker per card and exits, so nothing ever ticks the store
profile_scaffold.py scaffolds to profiles/platform/cron/jobs.json: that
directory holds jobs.json, executions.db and a .jobs.lock, but none of the
ticker's own files (.tick.lock, ticker_heartbeat, ticker_last_success),
which exist only under the Chat Agent's HERMES_HOME/cron/. A job left here
is therefore inert — it sits in a roster nothing reads, which is how six
governance watchdogs went a release without firing.
Those six now live in agents/chat/defaults/cron/jobs.json as `no_agent`
script entries. Each runs agents/chat/scripts/dispatch_<id>.py on the Chat
Agent's ticker, which files a kanban card assigned to this profile. The
work is still the Platform Agent's; only the clock moved.
Emptying this file does not empty an existing cluster's copy of it. The
start-up merge in profile_scaffold.py adds and overwrites but never
prunes, so an upgraded volume keeps the entries it was given, and
cronjob(action='list') will still show them there. Harmless, for the same
reason the jobs moved: with no ticker, no leftover fires.
Hermes ignores every top-level key but `jobs` when it loads the store, so
this note is inert too.
